A working prototype of the MIP*=RE compression step

Compress, Explained

Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright and Yuen prove MIP* = RE by building a machine that eats a verifier's source code and returns a verifier that does the same job exponentially faster. This page is a tour of that machine as we have actually built it in Julia — every instrument below runs on objects the test suite printed, and every number is stamped with what it is allowed to claim.

The one law of this page: nothing is stated more strongly than claims/CLAIMS.md allows. Two chapters describe machinery that is designed but has not yet run (introspection, and the end-to-end Compress); they say so in the margin, in the figure, and in the text. Sixteen instruments, six clips, one machine room.

§1

Turing machinesdocs/analytic part1a §1.2

A verifier is a finite transition table. Everything the paper says about its code, time and simulation refers to this object.

The analytic document opens with a machine so small it fits in five rows: M₌, which reads one bit off each of two input tapes and writes their equality bit to an output tape. It has two non-halting states and one halting state, four tapes, and a catch-all row that makes the table total. On legal one-bit inputs it halts after exactly three transitions.

Instrument · the equality machinepart1a §1.2 · five rows, verbatim

Configuration (q, (L, s, R)) per tape: the amber cell is the scanned symbol s, the strings left and right of it are L and R. The rule that fires is named beneath.

What the paper needs from this

A verifier's description ⟨V⟩ is a finite string spelling out such a table, and Time counts transitions. Compression is a statement about that string and that count — not about the function the machine computes. A universal machine U reading ⟨M⟩ and x simulates M on x; the whole construction is bookkeeping about how long that takes and how long the strings are.

§2

Lambda terms and quotationpart1b §3–§4C18 SKETCH

Recursion is not a name pointing at itself. It is a finite term that grows only when you run it.

The self-referential verifier at the heart of the Halting reduction is a fixed point. In the lambda calculus that is Y = λF.(λx.F(xx))(λx.F(xx)): no recursive name appears anywhere in the syntax, and recursion is produced when two copies meet. The project's evaluator is deterministic call-by-value, so its constructor must behave like the eta-delayed Z, and the implementation closes a single self_code hole rather than materialising the unfolding.

Instrument · β-reduction with de Bruijn indicespart1b §4.3 · λx.λy.x y ≡ λ.λ.(1 0)

A bound occurrence is replaced by the number of binders between it and its binder, counting the nearest as zero. Both λa.λb.a b and λx.λy.x y serialise to the same tree — which is why canonical bytes exist at all, and why inserting a closed term can never capture a name.

Instrument · the real 33 bytessrc/ir/programs.jl · TB3 · fnv1a64 f8561ef8c5761695

This is the canonical serialisation of the trivial decider λ n x y a b . true, printed by the package. Hover or focus a byte to see what field it belongs to.

Every field is prefix-free: a tag byte, then fixed-width big-endian counts, then children. Decoding is total; decode_cl and decode_program invert it exactly.

What is claimed, and what is not

C18 (SKETCH) records the s-m-n transformer, Kleene's e_Q = s(p,p), and the statement that the paper's explicit F(F,M,λ,…), the Kleene fixed point and DM,λ = YCode(ΨM,λ) are three descriptions of the same partial function, all of size O(|M| + log λ + 1). That is a written derivation, not a verified one. The extensional fixed-point value argument stays CITED. Note also that §8's constant is c_Y = 3 while the TB3 implementation charges c_Y = 1 — TB3 is evidence for that instantiation, not for §8's constants.

§3

Fuel and the CEK machinepart2a §8.5C16 SKETCH

Every reduction costs one unit. That is what turns "number of steps" into a resource the compression theorem can budget.

Evaluation is a deterministic call-by-value CEK machine with a fuel counter. One charged transition is one fuel unit, so a bounded trace has exactly one row per unit spent. Running out is not an error — it is the outcome OutOfFuel, alongside Value and SortError. The evaluator never throws.

What is claimed, and what is not

C16 (SKETCH): the CEK relation is a function, so evaluation is single-valued; fuel is monotone; and Eval_L(Quote(t), u; f + h(d,u)) = eval_L(t, u; f). TB3's tests (a) and (b) are the first machine evidence for it — on fixtures, with a coarser charge than §8's, byte units rather than the ν-encoding's bits, and c_Y = 1. There is no verdict promoting C16, so it stays SKETCH.

§4

Descriptions, not closuresgt-04-cl.tex def:samplerC4a TESTED

Compress consumes code. A Julia closure with a hidden environment is not code, and the type system says so out loud.

This is the requirement that shapes the whole prototype. Compress must measure a verifier's length, substitute static parameters into it, and emit new code — so a runtime function value will not do. Every sampler in the package is therefore asked four questions, and a sampler that cannot answer them from its own bytes is returned as NotDescribable rather than silently working.

what the round trip actually checks

decode_cl inverts canonical_bytes; the suite asserts canonical_bytes(describe_cl(decode_cl(b))) == b, apply(decode_cl(b), z) == apply(L, z) on all 8⁵ seeds, and equal depth-3 factor spaces. An independently written parser and evaluator — not the package's decoder — reproduced 648 comparisons with 0 disagreements at TB2.

Scope, verbatim: the bytes are not yet checked to carry the stage-matrix index order — every matrix serialised at this rung is diagonal, so a transposed encoder changes no described map and no test notices.

Why the paper cares

The compression machine's output sampler must depend only on λ and universal constants — never on the input verifier's bytes — or the recursion does not close. That is a statement about code dependencies, and it can only be tested on objects that have code.

§5

Conditionally linear samplersgt-07-ldt.tex:203–237C4a TESTED

The question distribution is not arbitrary: a seed is read in stages, and each stage's linear map may depend only on what earlier stages produced.

This is the structural constraint the whole construction is organised around. A conditionally linear map of level ℓ splits the ambient space into ℓ factor registers; it reads the first, applies a linear map to it, and only then chooses the linear map for the second. For (q,m,d) = (8,2,1) the ambient space is Vpt ⊕ Vcoord ⊕ Vdir, of dimension 5, and the three maps of the low-degree test sit at levels 1, 2 and 3.

§6

The classical low-degree testgt-07-ldt.tex fig:ld-deciderC4c TESTED

Ask for a point and a line through it. A cheating prover must either break the degree bound or contradict itself where they meet.

Claim C4c was created at TESTED by verdicts/tb1-r6.md (the TB1 lane's closing round, PASS). Along the way the r5 critic found a genuine divergence from the ground truth — on a zero-direction diagonal line the decider compared the line answer at t = 0 only, where gt-07-ldt.tex:379–384 requires every t; 1,024 of the 37,888 line-vs-point decisions — which brief 65 fixed source-exactly. One MINOR residue stands in the row's scope: the admissible set on a degenerate line is asserted, not yet mutation-owned.

The decider Dld sees two typed questions and two answers. If the types are equal it demands equal answers. If one is a point and the other a line through that point, it demands that the line polynomial has degree at most d (axis) or md (diagonal) and that evaluating it at the point reproduces the point answer. If nothing applies, it accepts.

One repair worth knowing about

The source accepts vacuously when no t with line(t) = point exists. The executable rejects instead — strictly stricter than the paper — and carries that decision as a SOURCE_REPAIR :ld_off_line_rejects node. The branch is reached zero times in the sweep, which is exactly why it needs a mutant of its own before anything may be claimed about it.

§7

Tseitin and arithmetizationgt-10-answer-reduction.tex prop:tseitin-arith-degreeC8 TESTED

Individual degree is fan-out. On the real six-gate circuit one variable reaches degree 6, not 2.

Tseitin turns a circuit into a formula by giving every gate a wire variable and asserting each gate's local relation; arithmetization turns that formula into a polynomial by sending ∧ to ×, ¬ to 1−·, and ∨ through De Morgan. The arithmetization of a formula tree is multilinear in its leaf occurrences, so a variable's individual degree is bounded by how many times it appears — which grows with the fan-out of the gate that produced it.

Instrument · the real six-gate TB0 circuitsrc/ir/circuits.jl tb0_circuit()

Click a wire variable to see where its occurrences come from. w₁ = ¬x₁ feeds both w₂ and w₃ — fan-out 2.

2 + 2·2 = 6
at the output wire w₆
3 + 2·0 = 3
two-gate regression (x₁,x₂,x₃,w₁,w₂)
(2, 2, 2, 4, 3)
Finding F1 — stated softly, on purposedocs/findings.md · C8 TESTED (scoped)

Our reading of the NW19 Tseitin gadget may be wrong. With that caveat first: reading z_i := (g_i ∧ w_i) ∨ (¬g_i ∧ ¬w_i) and arithmetizing along the formula tree gives occ(w_i) = 2 + 2·fanout(gate i) and occ(x_j) = 2·fanout(input j), so a fan-out-2 gate already reaches individual degree 6. The proposition in gt-10 states 2.

The theorem survives. The surviving weaker statement is deg_v(F_arith) ≤ 2(1 + fanout_max); with copy gates enforcing fan-out ≤ 2 that is ≤ 6, so c₀ has individual degree ≤ 7 and the Schwartz–Zippel bounds become (6+5d)m′/q and (2+d)m′/q — fine as long as d ≥ 7, and the paper's d = k ≥ 11. The individual-degree-3 statement for c₀ in the completeness proof inherits the same correction.

A second note, F2: NW19's F := z₁ ∧ … ∧ z_s constrains w to be the wire values but never asserts the output wire is 1, so it is satisfiable for every x. The MIP*=RE definition states the contract rather than the construction, so the implementation adds the conjunct w_out — one more occurrence, giving 3 + 2·fanout.

Exactly what C8 is allowed to say

TESTED, and scoped: the individual degrees of a real Tseitin arithmetization were computed, they equal the occurrence counts, and the mutants that would hide the discrepancy are killed. It is not a claim that the paper is wrong — it is a claim about what this arithmetization does on these circuits.

§8

The zero basisgt-10-answer-reduction.tex prop:zero-basisC2 TESTED

"Vanishes on the Boolean cube" becomes a coefficient identity — an object the verifier can check with a handful of point queries.

The PCP's central object is a polynomial c₀ built so that it vanishes on {0,1}n exactly when the underlying circuit is satisfied. Vanishing on the cube is equivalent to lying in the ideal generated by z_i(1 − z_i), so the prototype divides c₀ by that ideal and keeps the quotients as part of the proof. If the division leaves a remainder, no certificate is issued.

What stays CITED

The general circuit / Tseitin / F_arith correspondence is cited, not proved here. What is machine-checked is the exhaustive 2¹⁶ truth table on this circuit, the rewrite on arbitrary GF(8) coefficients, and the three witnesses. The 1,024-witness loop is a clause-relation count (512 satisfying) — a surrogate, explicitly not a remainder computation.

§9

The PCP verifiergt-10-answer-reduction.tex fig:pcpverifierC1 TESTED

Five low-degree extensions, one polynomial that must vanish on the cube, and a verifier that reads a handful of points and lines.

The proof string is Π = (g₁,…,g₅, c₀, c₁,…,c_{m′}): five low-degree extensions of the witness blocks, the composite polynomial, and its quotients. The verifier picks a random point, restricts the proof to axis-parallel and diagonal lines through it, checks degrees, and then checks two algebraic identities — the formula test and the zero-on-subcube test. Everything below is measured on the six-gate instance.

the budget, honestly

Witness (i) has 33,432 monomials in c₀; the five per-block products cost 37,240 / 33,432 / 33,432 / 33,432 / 33,432, so the cumulative 170,968 exceeds the 160,000-monomial budget while the peak 37,240 does not. The builder therefore streams rather than materialising — and when a real generated instance blows the budget it says ExpansionRefused instead of allocating (chapter 11).

the policy report, verbatim

policy γ=1
small = (PASS, FAIL, FAIL, FAIL, FAIL, FAIL)
sampled = (PASS, NOT_EVALUABLE, PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS)
degree_formula = 6

Failed hypotheses are printed as FAIL and unmeasured costs as NOT_EVALUABLE; neither is ever folded into a PASS. That discipline is what makes the toy-regime chapters below readable at all.

What C1 is and is not

It is completeness evidence on named points and lines, replayed node by node from the constructor's own sub-terms, with an object-identity check so a certificate borrowed from another proof is refused with :certificate_binding. It is not an exhaustive all-z statement and not a soundness claim. No uniform z in GF(2¹¹)¹⁶ are sampled — that gap is tracked as an open issue.

§10

Answer reductiongt-10-answer-reduction.tex fig:decider-pcpC9, C4b TESTED

Three roles times eighteen question types is 2,916 ordered pairs — and on 2,736 of them the decider is required to check nothing at all.

Answer reduction replaces long answers with short ones by making the provers answer a PCP about their own long answers. The verifier's question type set becomes a product: each of the three oracularised roles (alice, bob, oracle) carries the eighteen PCP question types {Point_i, ALine_i, DLine_i}i=1..6. The decider is a dispatch table over the resulting 54 types, and the striking fact is how sparse it is.

the gap that is still open

The 54 product maps are NotDescribable: direct_sum wraps host closures. Their four queries and the lem:cl-kth replay do work, but description-level DL9-direct-sum is not implemented. So the typed layer is describable and the product layer is not — and the compression recursion needs the product layer.

The detyping "+2 levels" and every quantum soundness statement remain CITED.

One load-bearing repair

eq:V-pcp gives dim V6,coord = 6 while table:tpcp supplies one scalar. The implementation reads Vaux,coord and zeroes the other five components — SOURCE_REPAIR :PCPCopy6CoordinateScalar. The convention is load-bearing: reading the copy-1 scalar instead makes step 4(c) reject.

§11

The quoted front endgt-10:237–273 prop:standard-succinct-satC10 TESTED · tb3-r2 FAIL(N11)

From 33 bytes of quoted decider to a PCP instance, with nothing hand-written in between.

Claim C10 was promoted to TESTED by verdicts/tb3-r2.md. One MAJOR remains open there (N11): it is the orchestrator's, not the code's — the instantiation clause on C16/C18 had been narrowed before adjudication and has since been corrected. The remaining minors (N12–N17) close inside the TB4 round.

This is the rung that makes the pipeline real: the decider is quoted to canonical bytes, evaluated under fuel to produce a bounded trace, the trace is turned into succinct 3SAT by a Cook–Levin encoding, the shared 3SAT data is decoupled into five blocks, the result is padded and compiled to a circuit, and that generated circuit goes through the same PCP builder chapter 8 used — and then through chapter 10's decider.

Instrument · the front end on two real decidersTB3 · all values printed by test/tb3_frontend.jl
The honest failurethe equality decider never reaches build_pcp

Three fuel units instead of one, and the instance explodes: 15 3SAT clauses become 47 decoupled 5SAT clauses (15 formula + 4 copy + 28 equality), the padded instance has 423 live gates against 3 for the trivial one, and the arithmetization refuses at the seventh gadget:

ExpansionRefused(279,936 > 160,000)

The refusal is the point. A budget that is silently exceeded produces a number nobody can trust; a budget that refuses produces a fact. The F_arith candidate count at that stage is bounded by 669·7423 ≈ 6.8 × 10412, and c₀ by about 2.2 × 10414 — so nothing here was going to be materialised.

The two leaves that are not CHECKED

[CITED] CookLevinGeneral — field alphabets are enumerated over all four answer inputs rather than decoded from an O(log T + log σ)-bit window, and the enc_Γ answer format is not enforced. [ASSUMED] RawAnswerBlocks — answer blocks are read as raw bits of widths 1, 1; the enc_Γ format and the (10)L/2−T padding clauses of gt-10:1036–1130 are not emitted. Both sit in the certificate tree where a reader can find them.

§12

Introspectiongt-08-introspection.texC14 CONJECTURE

The verifier stops sending questions and instead asks the provers to sample their own — which only works because entanglement lets it check that they sampled honestly.

designed, not yet executable

Everything in this chapter is transcribed into docs/DESIGN.md §11 with source line references, and nothing in it has run. It is here because it is the piece that makes compression exponential: a verifier of index n would need 2n-bit questions, so instead the provers are made to generate their own questions from shared randomness, and the verifier checks the generation with a Pauli test.

Instrument · the Pauli basis and the 3Q boundaryDESIGN §11.1–§11.4 · design only

Two provers share EPR pairs and are asked to measure in the X or the Z basis. Anticommuting observables cannot both be determined; the test uses exactly that to certify the measurement, not the outcome.

The fuel gate, and why it is not a formalitygt-08-introspection.tex:417–419

Every call the introspection decider makes into the input verifier — sampler or decider, including Dimension(N) — gets exactly R = Nλ units, and the counter rejects before executing step R+1; a return at step R is permitted. λ-boundedness is two separate conditions — a byte-size bound on |V| and a runtime bound — and neither discharges the other. The design records that every child-call record must carry fixture, quote hash, mode, role, stage, exact metered cost, the source R, the supplied budget, and the timeout/return; until a quoted-interpreter trace exists, costs stay NOT_EVALUABLE(owner=tb6-child-meter) and no dependent acceptance may pass.

Status, precisely

C14 is a CONJECTURE, authorised as such by verdicts/design-v2-r3.md. The Pauli decider's predicates are ordinary field, polynomial-evaluation, parity and equality calls, so they would be executable; quantum rigidity — the actual content of thm:pauli — is not part of that predicate and remains CITED.

§13

Anchoring and repetitiongt-11-parallel-repetition.texC13 TESTED

Compression costs soundness; parallel repetition buys it back — and the toy diagnostic in this repo shows why naive repetition cannot.

executed at TB5 — C13 TESTED (scoped), C12 TESTED

Each stage of Compress degrades the soundness gap, so the last stage restores it by running k(n) copies in parallel. Anchoring comes first: a second question type whose only legal answer is the canonical bit 0, which gives the repetition theorem the structure it needs. TB5 built both as description-level transformations: the anchored sampler on the V_copy fixture has level 3 and dimension 9, the 81-fold repetition is one compact loop term of 85 bytes whose size does not change with k, the repeated decider computes the component bound before reading any payload and rejects an oversized component with an empty child-call log, and two byte-distinct deciders yield the identical repeated-sampler hash. What stays CITED is exactly what the paper proves analytically: PCC completeness and the entanglement relation of thm:repetition.

Instrument · the 81-fold direct sumDESIGN §10.3 · TB5 fixture · executed: |S^rep| = 85 bytes, 128/128 honest pairs, four named transcripts

The repeated decider takes the logical AND of the copies, so one corrupted component rejects the whole transcript. It also computes the component bound B(n) = (λn)τ before reading any payload, so a hostile length prefix cannot force an unbounded scan.

The diagnostic that rules out the naive routeC6, N1 — both PROVED

The one thing on this page with a proved status is a negative result. A recursive midpoint protocol verifies y = f2ⁿ(x) in O(n) verifier time and has perfect completeness — but for a false claim the optimal acceptance probability is exactly 1 − 2−n, and adaptive r-copy sequential repetition gives exactly (1 − 2−n)r. So amplification needs Θ(2ⁿ) repetitions and destroys the compression. That is the precise sense in which an iteratable, gap-preserving transformation is the hard requirement.

C6 and N1 are PROVED via verdicts/midpoint-r2.md, with 1,380 exact values checked over ℤ/5 and friends. The verdict struck the stronger phrasing "cannot serve as a compression step" (objection O15) — the negative result is about sequential repetition.

A source inconsistency the code refuses to smooth over

gt-12:70 prints k(n) = (λn)τ inside ComputeParrepVerifier, conflicting with gt-11:200 and gt-12:355, which both say (λn)(1+c′)τ. The description retains the latter two and reports the inconsistent line without using it. The source also calls k(n) an integer while declaring only c′ > 0; production keeps the symbolic term plus an ASSUMED integrality witness rather than silently rounding.

D = Y Ψ, and the last stephandoff.md · gt-12-compression.tex:426–492

Now the fixed point. Define, for a machine M and a bound λ,

ΨM,λ(d)(n, x, y, a, b) = 1  if M halts within n steps,
                       = DCompress((Sλ, d), λ)(n, x, y, a, b)  otherwise.

Then DM,λ = Y ΨM,λ. If M never halts, the verifier at index n defers to the compressed verifier at a larger index, forever, and the game has a perfect entangled strategy at every level; if M halts at step T, the deferral bottoms out and the value drops. Deciding the value of the game therefore decides the halting problem — which is MIP* = RE.

Chapter 2's Y is exactly this combinator, and the implementation's Fix closes one self_code hole at constant charge rather than materialising the unfolding — which is what keeps |DM,λ| = O(|M| + log λ + 1) instead of unbounded. The TB7 run is specified to construct Fix(ΨM,λ), check that the embedded self_code hash equals the outer quote hash, simulate two steps of a non-halting M_loop, take the deferral branch, and execute the compressed decider without recursive host evaluation. It has not been run.

What this page does not claim. One description-level self-reference is not the infinite fixed-point value argument. The general value and λ-bounded conclusions of gt-12:502–519, 569–576 stay CITED, and so does every quantitative soundness and entanglement-dimension bound in the composition.

§15

How these claims were earnedverdicts/ · test/mutations/

A status only ever rises because an adversarial critic said so, and every green test has a mutant proving it can go red.

Each rung of the ladder is written by a proposer and then attacked by a critic that recomputes the numbers independently. The critic files a verdict with numbered objections; the proposer repairs; the next critic adjudicates the repairs and files fresh objections. A claim's status moves up only inside such a verdict — never because the author says so.

Objection trajectories, by lane25 verdict files · MAJOR objections, the count each verdict itself tracks

Seven lanes converged to zero MAJOR objections and a PASS. Three are still open: TB3 at FAIL(N11) after two rounds, TB4 at FAIL(O1–O5) after one, TB5 at FAIL(O1,O2) after one. No verdict line ever reads PROMOTE — only PASS or FAIL(…); promotions live inside the per-claim decision sections.

The mutation runnerbaseline-first, each mutant in an isolated copy

Before any mutant runs, the runner establishes that the targeted test file passes unmutated — 43 baselines. Then each of the 84 registered mutants is applied in isolation and the target must exit non-zero. A mutant that survives is a test that proves nothing; a mutant that kills the wrong test is recorded as UNATTRIBUTABLE rather than counted. This run: no survivors, no load errors, nothing unattributable.

§16

The certificate treesrc/certificates.jl

Every bound in the prototype carries a derivation tree, and the leaves say honestly which of them were only cited.

Nothing returns a bare number. A construction returns a Checked{T,C} — the term together with a certificate whose nodes are graded. verify_certificate replays every CHECKED node against the constructor's own sub-terms, and refuses a certificate borrowed from another proof with :certificate_binding. These are the two real trees the suite printed.

Instrument · the trees, as printeddata/suite59q.log · click a node

Select a node to see its grade, what it asserts, and where its authority comes from.

CHECKED replayed from the constructor's own sub-terms CONSTRUCTED true by the datatype's invariants CITED an analytic theorem, not reproduced here ASSUMED a gap the code does not fill SOURCE_REPAIR the source as written does not typecheck; this is the repair
The point of the grades

A tree in which every leaf is CHECKED would be a lie. The value of the discipline is that CookLevinGeneral is visibly CITED, RawAnswerBlocks is visibly ASSUMED, and the five SOURCE_REPAIR nodes are visibly repairs — so a reader can locate exactly where this prototype stops being evidence and starts being transcription.
